newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe vows all-out effort to solve attack.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe vows all-out effort to solve attack.

text.p: Prime Minister Alain Juppe vowed on Wednesday an all-out effort to identify and bring to justice the perpetrators of a rush-hour bomb on a Paris commuter train and said it bore striking similarities to last year's attacks by Algerian Moslem fundamentalists.

"Everything possible will be done to identify and punish those responsible for the attack. We will do all we can to protect our fellow citizens," Juppe told the National Assembly in a solemn statement on the blast in which two people died and 79 were injured.

Deputies stood for a moment's silence at the start of question time in a show of respect for the victims of Tuesday's bombing of an RER commuter train at the Port Royal station on the Left Bank of central Paris.

Officials said the bomb was a 13-kg (29-lb) gas canister packed with nails and explosive, the same type of device used in last year's bombings. The choice of target and the timing of the attack also were similar to some of last year's bombings.

"No one has claimed responsibility. No particular theory can be privileged. But that said, striking similarities exist between this attack and the conditions in which the attacks of summer 1995 were committed," Juppe said.

He said an interministerial anti-terrorism committee would meet on Wednesday afternoon. President Jacques Chirac earlier discussed security measures with senior ministers and the government said 1,800 soldiers would bolster police in tightening security at borders and public places across France.
